modules.name: Core
modules.description: Tenant identity, Site scope, publishing, versioning, audit and shared platform primitives required by every NEXT F Site.

modules.name: Media
modules.description: Reusable Site-scoped media library and asset metadata used by content and commerce without tying contracts to one storage provider.

dependencies.reason: Media assets are Site-scoped and audited through Core.

modules.name: Pages
modules.description: Structured pages, sections, reusable content, navigation, legal content and custom collections for coded customer websites.

dependencies.reason: All page content is Site-scoped and publishable.
Page blocks may reference canonical media assets.
Routable pages should normally use canonical SEO metadata.

modules.name: Blog
modules.description: Editorial publishing for Blog Posts, categories, tags, authors, related posts, scheduling and approval workflows.

dependencies.reason: Blog content uses Core publishing/versioning.
Blog posts use canonical media references.
Published posts should normally use canonical SEO metadata.

modules.name: Documentation
modules.description: Structured documentation collections, categories and articles with attachments, visibility, related content and version-aware publishing.

dependencies.reason: Documentation is versioned and Site-scoped.
Documentation may reference attachments/media.
Public documentation benefits from canonical SEO metadata.

modules.name: SEO
modules.description: Canonical metadata, keywords, social metadata, structured data, redirects, sitemap, robots, audits and search-performance records.

dependencies.reason: SEO records belong to a Site and target canonical entities.
Search performance and indexing data may be sourced through supported connectors.

modules.name: Forms
modules.description: Structured forms, submissions, validation, notifications, spam handling, consent capture and conversion mapping.

dependencies.reason: Forms and submissions are Site-scoped.
Consent module is required when optional analytics/marketing consent is collected or enforced.

modules.name: Leads
modules.description: Lead records, status, assignment, notes, activity, deduplication and export generated from approved sources such as Forms.

dependencies.reason: Leads are Site-scoped business records.
Phase 17 Lead workflows use the Forms/Lead contract family as their canonical source.

modules.name: Consent
modules.description: Tracking and marketing consent preferences, states, policies and immutable consent records used to gate optional integrations.

dependencies.reason: Consent state is Site-scoped and auditable.

modules.name: Analytics
modules.description: Provider-neutral website measurement, analytics observations, reporting, attribution and campaign performance summaries.

dependencies.reason: Analytics configuration is Site-scoped.
Optional analytics measurement must honor canonical consent state.
Provider reporting normally arrives through supported integration connectors.

modules.name: Marketing
modules.description: Conversions, campaign attribution, UTM/click identifiers, marketing destinations and provider-neutral tracking configuration.

dependencies.reason: Marketing configuration is Site-scoped.
Optional marketing destinations must honor consent.
Attribution and reporting can consume Analytics capability.
Ad platforms and marketing tools connect through canonical connectors.

modules.name: Integrations
modules.description: Approved provider connectors, credentials references, environment bindings, mappings, synchronization and health diagnostics.

dependencies.reason: Connections are Site-scoped and permission-controlled.
Tracking/advertising connectors require consent-aware runtime behavior.

modules.name: Commerce
modules.description: Full transactional commerce foundation covering catalog, inventory, customers, cart, checkout, orders, payments, fulfillment, discounts, returns, reviews and tax/shipping models.

dependencies.reason: Commerce requires tenant scope, audit and authoritative Site identity.
Catalog products and commerce content may reference canonical media.
Product/category storefront content should use canonical SEO.
Commerce sites frequently enable analytics/marketing consent.
Payment, shipping, tax and marketing providers connect through canonical integrations.
